answer: Medicare usually doesn't cover cosmetic surgery, but repair of your face after a serious car crash is not treated as excluded cosmetic surgery when it is prompt repair of an accidental injury. The repair must be prompt (i.e., as soon as medically feasible). The passages do not state what deductible, coinsurance, or prior-authorization steps apply to this facial repair.

citations.quote: Cosmetic surgery includes any surgical procedure directed at improving appearance, except when required for the prompt (i.e., as soon as medically feasible) repair of accidental injury
this exclusion does not apply to surgery in connection with treatment of severe burns or repair of the face following a serious automobile accident
Medicare usually doesn’t cover cosmetic surgery unless you need it because of accidental injury or to improve the function of a malformed body part.

gold_answer: It is covered. Cosmetic surgery is excluded, but surgery needed for prompt repair of an accidental injury or to improve the function of a malformed body part is not treated as cosmetic, and repair of the face after a serious automobile accident is given as an example.
gold_quote: Cosmetic surgery includes any surgical procedure directed at improving appearance, except when required for the prompt (i.e., as soon as medically feasible) repair of accidental injury or for the improvement of the functioning of a malformed body member. For example, this exclusion does not apply to surgery in connection with treatment of severe burns or repair of the face following a serious automobile accident, or to surgery for therapeutic purposes which coincidentally also serves some cosmetic purpose.

judge.rationale: The answer says facial repair after a serious car crash is not treated as excluded cosmetic surgery when it is prompt repair of an accidental injury, which matches the gold answer and is stated in P1 and P2.

question: Will Medicare pay for surgery to fix my face after a bad car crash, or is that considered cosmetic?
